ei.subject: 2025년 9월 고1 모의고사
ei.title: May I Help You? — Building Trust with Customers

fullPassage:
"May I help you?" are the worst four words that a retail salesperson can utter because they don't encourage the customer to talk and put them on the defensive. The four words usually draw out a negative response that stops cold a sales transaction. Examples of (a) better questions to use when approaching customers are "Is there anything in particular that you are looking for?" and "Are you shopping for a gift?" If a fashion salesperson approached you with "May I help you?" chances are you would feel the salesperson didn't (b) care. This line is a rote approach that is so overused by untrained and uninterested salespeople. In fact, most of us shudder in horror on hearing these words. The very meaning of the question "May I help you?" (c) rejects the customer is in trouble of some sort and needs rescuing. This almost always puts the customer on the defense. "No, thank you" is usually the immediate response, even if the customer is actually in need of assistance. The subconscious thought by the customer is often "I'm smart enough to figure out what I want, and I don't need your help!"
If customers feel pressured or cornered, then salespeople won't make any sales. The approach has to promote a (d) comfortable environment that makes customers feel there is no rush. Furthermore, if customers just want to look around, they should feel that it is all right to do so. In situations where customers really do want to look around on their own, salespeople should give customers their business cards and keep themselves (e) accessible in case customers have questions or concerns.

questions.passage: "May I help you?" are the worst four words that a retail salesperson can (A)[utter / silence] because they don't encourage the customer to talk and put them on the defensive. The four words usually draw out a negative response that stops cold a sales transaction. Examples of better questions to use when approaching customers are "Is there anything in particular that you are looking for?" This line is a rote approach that is so (B)[overused / underused] by untrained and uninterested salespeople. The approach has to promote a comfortable environment that makes customers feel there is no (C)[rush / delay].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① utter — overused — rush: 원문 일치
❌ ② silence는 '침묵시키다'로 반의어
❌ ③ underused는 '덜 사용된'으로 반의어
❌ ④ delay는 '지연'으로 문맥 부적절
det.tip: utter(말하다) ↔ silence(침묵시키다), overused(남용된) ↔ underused(거의 안 쓰인)

The very meaning of the question "May I help you?" rejects the customer is in trouble of some sort and needs rescuing. This almost always puts the customer on the (B)[defense / offense]. If customers feel (C)[pressured / relaxed] or cornered, then salespeople won't make any sales.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ encourage — defense — pressured: 원문 일치
❌ ① discourage는 반의어
❌ ② offense는 '공격'으로 반의어
❌ ④ relaxed는 반의어
det.tip: encourage ↔ discourage, defense ↔ offense, pressured ↔ relaxed

The very meaning of the question "May I help you?" rejects the customer is in trouble of some sort and needs (A)[rescuing / abandoning]. "No, thank you" is usually the (B)[immediate / delayed] response, even if the customer is actually in need of assistance. The (C)[subconscious / conscious] thought by the customer is often "I'm smart enough to figure out what I want, and I don't need your help!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② rescuing — immediate — subconscious: 원문 일치
❌ ① abandoning은 '포기'로 반의어
❌ ③ delayed는 반의어
❌ ④ conscious는 '의식적인'으로 반의어
det.tip: subconscious(잠재의식) ↔ conscious(의식적인), immediate(즉각적) ↔ delayed(지연된)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ①②③ 원문 일치
✅ ④ hostile(적대적인)은 comfortable(편안한)의 반의어. 서두르지 않는 편안한 환경을 만들어야 한다는 맥락
det.tip: comfortable(편안한) ↔ hostile(적대적인)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ inaccessible → accessible: 고객이 질문할 때 접근 가능해야 한다

✅ ④ inaccessible(접근불가)은 accessible(접근가능)의 반의어. 고객이 질문이 있을 때 접근 가능해야 한다는 맥락

questions.passage: Examples of better questions to use when ①<u>approaching</u> customers are "Is there anything in particular that you are looking for?" and "Are you shopping for a gift?" This line is a ②<u>rote</u> approach that is so overused by untrained and uninterested salespeople. In fact, most of us shudder in ③<u>delight</u> on ④<u>hearing</u> these words. Furthermore, if customers just want to look around, they should feel that it is all right to do so.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ delight → horror: 이 말을 듣고 공포로 몸서리치는 것이지 기쁨이 아님
det.analysis:
❌ ①② 원문 일치
✅ ③ delight(기쁨)는 horror(공포)의 반의어. shudder(몸서리치다)와 결합하면 horror가 자연스러움
det.tip: shudder in horror(공포로 몸서리치다) — delight(기쁨)와 shudder는 어울리지 않음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: rescuing(구조) — 고객이 곤경에 처해 구조가 필요하다는 의미
det.analysis:
✅ ② rescuing: 고객이 trouble에 처해 있고 구조가 필요하다는 문맥
❌ ① purchasing: 구매는 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ avoiding: 피하기는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ entertaining: 즐겁게 하기는 문맥과 무관
det.tip: in trouble + needs rescuing = 곤경에 처해 구조가 필요하다

questions.passage: If customers feel pressured or cornered, then salespeople won't make any sales. The approach has to promote a comfortable environment that makes customers feel there is no rush. Furthermore, if customers just want to look around, they should feel that it is all right to do so. In situations where customers really do want to look around on their own, salespeople should give customers their business cards and keep themselves __________ in case customers have questions or concerns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: accessible(접근 가능한) — 고객이 필요할 때 접근할 수 있어야 함
det.analysis:
✅ ③ accessible: 명함을 주고 접근 가능 상태를 유지하라는 맥락
❌ ① invisible: 보이지 않으면 도움 불가
❌ ② aggressive: 공격적이면 고객이 불편
❌ ④ indifferent: 무관심하면 서비스 불가
det.tip: accessible = 접근 가능한. keep oneself accessible = 접근 가능한 상태를 유지하다

questions.passage: "May I help you?" are the worst four words that a retail salesperson can utter. The four words usually draw out a negative response that stops cold a sales transaction. This line is a __________ approach that is so overused by untrained and uninterested salespeople. In fact, most of us shudder in horror on hearing these words. "No, thank you" is usually the immediate response, even if the customer is actually in need of assistance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: rote(판에 박힌) — 훈련받지 않은 판매원이 남용하는 기계적 접근법
det.analysis:
✅ ④ rote: 판에 박힌 기계적 접근법, overused와 어울림
❌ ① creative: 창의적이라면 overused와 모순
❌ ② innovative: 혁신적이라면 worst와 모순
❌ ③ personalized: 개인 맞춤이라면 문맥과 반대
det.tip: rote = 기계적인, 판에 박힌. rote learning = 암기식 학습

questions.passage: "May I help you?" are the worst four words that a retail salesperson can <u>utter</u> because they don't encourage the customer to talk and put them on the defensive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>utter</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② say: utter와 동의어 (말하다)
❌ ① whisper: 속삭이다 — 뉘앙스 다름
❌ ③ deny: 부인하다 — 의미 다름
❌ ④ repeat: 반복하다 — 의미 다름
det.tip: utter = say, speak, express (말하다, 발언하다)

questions.passage: The four words usually draw out a negative response that stops cold a sales transaction. This almost always puts the customer on the defense. The <u>subconscious</u> thought by the customer is often "I'm smart enough to figure out what I want."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>subconscious</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ unconscious: 잠재의식적인과 가장 유사
❌ ① deliberate: 의도적인 — 반의어
❌ ② rational: 이성적인 — 다른 의미
❌ ④ obvious: 명백한 — 다른 의미
det.tip: subconscious(잠재의식) ≈ unconscious(무의식) ↔ conscious(의식적인)

questions.passage: The approach has to <u>promote</u> a comfortable environment that makes customers feel there is no rush. Furthermore, if customers just want to look around, they should feel that it is all right to do so.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>promote</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② foster: 조성하다, 촉진하다 — promote와 동의어
❌ ① prevent: 방지하다 — 반의어
❌ ③ eliminate: 제거하다 — 반의어
❌ ④ restrict: 제한하다 — 반의어
det.tip: promote ≈ foster ≈ encourage (촉진하다, 조성하다)

questions.passage: If customers feel pressured or <u>cornered</u>, then salespeople won't make any sales. The approach has to promote a comfortable environment that makes customers feel there is no rush.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 cornered와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ free: 자유로운 — cornered의 반의어
❌ ① trapped: 갇힌 — 동의어
❌ ② confined: 갇힌 — 동의어
❌ ④ restricted: 제한된 — 유의어
det.tip: cornered = trapped = confined (궁지에 몰린) ↔ free(자유로운)

questions.passage: This line is a rote approach that is so overused by untrained and <u>uninterested</u> salespeople. In fact, most of us shudder in horror on hearing these words.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 uninterested와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ enthusiastic: 열정적인 — 관심과 열의를 보이는 것
❌ ① apathetic: 무관심한 — 동의어
❌ ② indifferent: 무관심한 — 동의어
❌ ③ bored: 지루해하는 — 유의어
det.tip: uninterested ≈ apathetic ≈ indifferent ↔ enthusiastic ≈ passionate

questions.passage:
(A) If a fashion salesperson approached you with "May I help you?" chances are you would feel the salesperson didn't <u>care</u>.

(B) In situations where customers really do want to look around on their own, salespeople should take <u>care</u> to give customers their business cards.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 <u>care</u>가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) care = 관심을 갖다, (B) care = 주의를 기울이다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 관심 — 주의: (A)는 '관심을 두다', (B)는 take care to = '~에 주의를 기울이다'
❌ ① 걱정 — 돌봄: 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ② 돌봄 — 관심: 순서 뒤바뀜
❌ ④ 주의 — 걱정: 순서 뒤바뀜
det.tip: care: (1) 관심/배려 (2) 주의(take care to) (3) 걱정(I don't care) (4) 돌봄(health care)

det.analysis:

questions.passage: "No, thank you" is usually the __________ (immediate) response, even if the customer is actually in need of assistance.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis:
✅ immediate: 명사 response를 수식하는 형용사 원형 그대로
* immediately(부사)로 바꾸면 안 됨 — response(명사) 앞 수식어는 형용사
det.tip: immediate(형용사) vs immediately(부사) — 명사 앞에는 형용사

questions.passage: In fact, most of us shudder in horror on __________ (hear) these words.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis:
✅ hearing: 전치사 on + 동명사(V-ing). on hearing = ~을 듣자마자
* hear(원형)나 heard(과거분사)는 전치사 뒤에 올 수 없음
det.tip: 전치사 + V-ing: on hearing(듣자마자), by reading(읽음으로써)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: in need of assistance(도움이 필요한 상태) — 실제로 도움이 필요해도 거절한다는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① in need of assistance: 도움이 필요한 상태지만 거절한다는 역설
❌ ② satisfied with the service: 만족하면 거절할 이유가 없어 문맥 부적합
❌ ③ ready to make a purchase: 구매 준비가 되었다면 even if와 모순
❌ ④ looking for a specific item: 문맥 흐름과 맞지 않음
det.tip: even if = 비록 ~일지라도. 도움이 필요해도 거절한다는 역설적 상황

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: keep themselves accessible in case customers have questions — 질문 대비 접근 가능 유지
det.analysis:
✅ ② keep themselves accessible in case customers have questions: 명함을 주고 필요할 때 접근 가능하게
❌ ① follow customers around the store: 따라다니면 pressured 느낌
❌ ③ immediately approach with more offers: 즉시 접근은 rush 분위기
❌ ④ leave the store for a break: 가게를 떠나면 서비스 불가
det.tip: keep oneself accessible = 접근 가능 상태 유지. in case = ~할 경우를 대비하여
